title: Add hybrid prefill+decode workload suite, golden baselines, and CI perf gates
creator: Alex Rivera
description:
Goal: Expand the benchmarking harness to cover mixed prefill + decode workload profiles that reflect our top 20 production request shapes, produce golden baseline artifacts for each model variant, and add deterministic CI perf gates to detect regressions in kernel selection, attention optimizations, and prefill/decoding scheduling.

Scope and deliverables:
- New workload suite: a set of 12 canonical mixed prefill/decode traces (prefill-length x decode-length combinations) derived from production sampling and synthetic edge cases.
- Golden baseline artifacts: reproducible runs (metrics + KV cache traces + config snapshot) stored under gs://redwood-bench/goldlines/runtime-1.20/ENG-15421/.
- CI perf gates: pipeline jobs that run a reduced subset (3 representative traces) on PRs affecting kernel routing, attention kernels, and scheduler code. Failures create auto-tickets and block merge.
- Docs + runbook: README, how-to-regenerate-golden, variance tolerance explanation, and remediation steps for failures.

Why this ticket: Current benchmarks are focused on pure prefill or microbench prefill scheduling. We see real customer workloads interleaving heavy prefill with bursty decode tails (long context + long decode), which changes kernel selection decisions and cache reuse behavior. Without a targeted mixed-suite, regressions slip through CI and manifest only in production.

Acceptance criteria (must be true for Done):
1) New workload suite implemented in benchmark harness and checked into repo under bench/suites/hybrid_prefill_decode/ with yaml definitions for each trace.
2) Golden baselines for each target model (gpt-xx small/med/large variants we serve) uploaded to the canonical GCS path with checksums and run metadata.
3) CI templates created (github actions + internal runner) that run the 3-PR-level traces and enforce thresholds (latency p95 and tokens/s drop) with clear error messages.
4) Documentation and runbook published: Confluence link and in-repo README.
5) Two end-to-end runs reproducing a regression scenario are recorded and attached to this ticket as artifacts.

Measurement definitions and thresholds (proposal):
- Primary metric: tokens_per_second (measured across decode window excluding prefill compute).
- Secondary metrics: p95 latency, avg GPU utilization, kernel-selection-change-rate (percent of steps where chosen kernel differs from baseline for same config).
- CI gate thresholds (for PR-level reduced traces): deny if tokens_per_second drops >8% from golden OR p95 latency increases >12% OR kernel-selection-change-rate >6%.
- Nightly full-suite tolerance: more lenient thresholds (drop >4% tokens/s triggers alert but not immediate rollback).

Workload composition (12 canonical traces):
- 4 short-prefill (128 tokens) x long-decode (512 tokens) shapes
- 4 mid-prefill (1024 tokens) x mid-decode (128 tokens) shapes
- 4 long-prefill (4096 tokens) x short-decode (32 tokens) shapes
Each trace annotated with model, batch size, typical sequence length histogram, and synthetic variation seeds. Traces are deterministic via seed & tokenizer versions.

Implementation approach:
- Bench harness changes: add trace loader that composes prefill+decode phases, reuses KV cache snapshots for reproducibility, and exports kernel selection logs per step.
- Golden generation: use pinned runtime-1.20 docker image + pinned NNPACK/cu versions; run on dedicated infra node with label bench-gold-1.
- CI gating: create a lightweight runner container with instrumented mini-runtime that reproduces kernel selection heuristics; run only 3 representative traces (one from each prefill-length bucket).
- Storage and reproducibility: store config json (env, kernel flags, compile flags), git sha, docker sha, and numeric seed for trace. Include checksums for trace input and outputs.

Trade-offs & decisions notes:
- We intentionally keep CI gate subset small to limit runtime costs; full suite runs nightly and on release candidates.
- Tighter thresholds on tokens/s could produce noisy false-positives; we picked conservative numbers based on 30 sample runs. Thresholds are configurable via bench/config/ci_thresholds.yaml.
- Golden runs require dedicated hardware variability control; will add a lab reservation step in the runbook to ensure consistent queueing.

Risks:
- Kernel selection is non-deterministic across minor driver updates; need to pin drivers in golden runs or accept higher variance.
- Storage of large golden artifacts occupies GCS budget; we stage only metric artifacts and compressed KV traces.

Artifacts & references:
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RUN/pages/Hybrid+Prefill+Decode+Suite (draft)
- Bench repo PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/482
- Draft runbook: gs://redwood-bench/docs/ENG-15421-runbook.md
- Example golden path: gs://redwood-bench/goldlines/runtime-1.20/ENG-15421/example-golden-20250226.tar.gz

Next steps / plan for this cycle:
- Week 1: finalize trace definitions and harness loader (owner: Maya)
- Week 2: run golden generation for two models and upload artifacts (owner: Suresh)
- Week 3: implement CI gate templates and test on a non-blocking branch (owner: Maya + CI infra)
- Week 4: docs, runbook and brief demos to PM and reliability teams (owner: Alex)
